title: High school orchestra and playing five nights a week
summary: He joined the high school orchestra, played dances five nights a week and summers at Harvey's Lake.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Okay, so you're still in high school.
Still in high school. Then I got in

the high school orchestra and that was a -- there were several who played jobs. guys there, several musicians there, A drummer who played quite a bit around, a piano player who played around quite a bit and we had another saxophone player there, a trumpet player.

-- one or two of the fiddle players -- They played around and they were quite good and they you know, seemed to fall right into it and they took me along. Called up and said, "We're going to play a job here or there," and the jobs at that time ran from 8:00 to 11:00, sometimes 8:00 to 12:00. So this allowed me to -- although my studies suffered -- this allowed me to stay out and play, stay home, in town. No traveling around.
There was a time there and business was quite good. The dance business. There were dances all over the places, so I worked on the average of five nights a week for quite awhile.
What did you do in the summertime?

Well, that's what I did, played in the evening. We have a lake near us they here, that's called Harvey's Lake and there were several pavillions that bands used to come there and played and the local bands would play. It was busy almost every night. There was one outfit there that ran the dances in those days every night but Sunday. Sunday -- Pennsylvania was known for -- couldn't play on Sunday -- its blue laws but I played with a group there, played the whole summer and camped over at the lake with the drummer, So I was getting fairly good, I mean competent, but my reading was

not very good. Just hadn't developed. As a matter of fact, you didn't do much reading. With a The band in those days, well, you were the 2 front-line guys, and the fiddle player with a (inaudible) and both of you maybe would do most of the improvising.
